record.paper_title: Option Pricing: Examples and Open Problems
record.original_question: An option price has a physical or realistic meaning for a writer when the amount lets the writer eliminate or at least shrink the possibility of bankruptcy and also gives the writer a good chance of profit. For a call option price C and put option price P on an underlying asset with current price S_0 and strike K, in the zero-interest setting the usual arbitrage-free constraints are S_0 - K < C < S_0, K - S_0 < P < K, and C - P = S_0 - K. Beyond the realistic binomial model, safe-price hedging, the (gamma + 1)-hedging strategy, and the Y/S_0-hedging strategy, what other realistic pricing and hedging methods can produce option prices with physical meaning?

evidence.quote: We say that the amount Y has a physical (or realistic) meaning for the writer if (i) with this amount the writer can eliminate or at least shrink the possibility of bankruptcy (ii) and moreover with this amount has a good chance of profit.
It is well known that the prices of the call and put option should satisfy the following inequalities in order to be free of arbitrage, S0 − K < C < S0 K − S0 < P < K C − P = S0 − K
It will be very interesting if we can find other, different from the above, realistic ways to price these options.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a European call and put option, with prices C and P respectively, written on an underlying risky asset whose current price is S_0 > 0, with strike price K > 0 and zero interest rate. Assume the no-arbitrage relations

  max(S_0 - K, 0) < C < S_0,    max(K - S_0, 0) < P < K,    C - P = S_0 - K.

Say that an amount Y has a physical (realistic) meaning for the writer of an option if: (i) using the amount Y the writer can eliminate or substantially reduce the possibility of bankruptcy from the obligation to deliver the option payoff at maturity, and (ii) with this amount the writer also has a positive (non-negligible) chance of making a profit.

Several pricing/hedging procedures are already known to produce option prices with such a physical meaning: the realistic binomial model, safe-price hedging, the (γ+1)-hedging strategy (for a suitable parameter γ), and the Y/S_0-hedging strategy (where the writer invests a fraction Y/S_0 of the received premium in the underlying asset).

Problem: Construct and analyze additional, genuinely different realistic pricing and hedging schemes for the call and put options above that yield prices C and P satisfying the arbitrage-free inequalities and put–call parity stated, and for which the prices have a physical meaning for the writer in the sense (i)–(ii). Specify the model assumptions on the price dynamics, describe the hedging portfolio, and verify both the bankruptcy-control property and the profit property.
artifact.status_search_result: No published resolution or comprehensive list of alternative realistic hedging methods (beyond the realistic binomial, safe-price, (γ+1)-, and Y/S_0-hedging strategies) appears in the available literature; the problem is posed as open and no follow-up work answering it was located.
